title: Fifteen Days and One Wrong Turning
subtitle: 旅行与见闻 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 旅行与见闻（社会服务与人际沟通·旅行与见闻）
meta: 主题语境：旅行与见闻（社会服务与人际沟通·旅行与见闻）　|　核心词汇：destination　|　正文 339 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 destination 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1949 the driver ① reached a destination that no map in the province would have shown, and he said the reaching was the whole of the journey. The ② destination, meaning the place and not the stop, ran fifteen days and stayed unnamed on the ticket; a destination, he said, is the only thing in a journey that is judged by how long it is left unprinted.

Every ③ destination on that road had the same wrong turning before it, and the ④ destination at the end, meaning the one they kept for the coast and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever asked for twice. A destination, his conductor said, is nine parts road and one part somebody willing to name; the driver said the naming is the part that fills fifteen days.

The clerk meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the destination was the whole of the timetable, meaning the stop and not the place. The ⑥ destination, meaning the stop and not any of that, is the only thing in a timetable that everybody prints and nobody explains; destination, he said, is either something you reach or the only word that means both a place and a stop. He said the stop is the part they remember.

By 1957 the ⑦ destination had become a line in a handbook, and the handbook had become an argument about the wrong turning. The ⑧ destination of the whole thing, the driver wrote in September, was one road and fifteen days of naming; destination, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to name. She said the naming was never mentioned.

The ⑨ destination I remember is the one at the end, which was reached in 1971 and is still described as the strangest on the road. A ⑩ destination, the conductor said in 1973, is the only thing that improves by being named; every destination, she said, is a stop that has agreed to look like a place. She said the stop was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 目的地；终点（指旅途上到达的那个地方）
B. n. 目的地（指那个地方本身，与那个站点相对）
C. 固定搭配：reach a destination 抵达一个目的地
D. n. 目的地（指留给海岸线那一段的那一个）
E. n. 目的地；终点（抽象总称，指一条路上的所有去处）
F. n. 目的地（指手册上印出、被列名的那一个）
G. n. 终点站；停靠站（指时刻表上印着的那一站）
H. n. 站点（抽象总称，指人人印出却无人解释的那一站）

answers.why: reach a destination 意为“抵达一个目的地”，1949 年司机抵达了一个全省没有一张地图画得出的目的地。
destination 意为“目的地”，指那个地方本身而不是那个站点，它走了十五天而在票上没有名字。
destination 意为“目的地”，指那条路上每一个目的地，每一个前面都有同一个错误的岔口。
destination 意为“目的地”，指留给海岸线那一段的那一个，是唯一有人问过两次的。
destination 意为“终点站、停靠站”，指时刻表上印着的那一站，售票员说这一站就是那份时刻表的全部。
destination 意为“站点”，指人人印出却无人解释的那一站而不是那个地方，是时刻表里人人都印出、却无人解释的东西。
destination 意为“目的地”，指手册上印出、被列名的那一个，到 1957 年这个目的地成了手册里的一行。
destination 意为“目的地、终点”，司机九月写道，整件事的终点是一条路和十五天的命名。
destination 意为“目的地”，我记得的是末尾那一个，1971 年抵达，至今仍被说成路上最奇的一个。
destination 为抽象总称，售票员 1973 年说，一个目的地是唯一会因为被叫出名字而变得更好的东西。
